page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a high-performance computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, delivering 48 physical cores with a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, meaning storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the server's capabilities in multi-threaded and memory-intensive workloads. The instance achieves top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU physics testing. Its DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier throughput, reaching 695.05 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 347.3 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Single-core performance remains strong, as evidenced by high scores in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core evaluations. Additionally, the platform demonstrates exceptional efficiency in database operations, processing 122.53 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the hpc7a.24xlarge offers a high-density compute and memory profile tailored for specialized workloads without the overhead of integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage. The high memory-to-core ratio of 16 GB per core makes it highly efficient for memory-bound parallel processing. This hardware configuration is optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) applications, large-scale scientific simulations, software compilation, memory-intensive database operations, and medium-scale language model inference.
